PaymentRefundedPayload.description: `payment.refunded`: the payment as v1 reads it right after the change (its `refund_status`, `refunded_amount`), and what moved it. An event is published only when `payment.refunded_amount` moved, and every move publishes one. Events can arrive late, twice or out of order, so the last one delivered is not always the newest: for the current figure, read `GET /v1/payments/{id}`. Over all of a payment's events, the sum of the signed `refund.applied_amount`, counted once per event id, is its `refunded_amount` minus what it was before its first event. That is 0 except for crypto refunds recorded before this event existed, which moved `refunded_amount` with no event. A running total kept from events therefore starts from a seed read from `GET /v1/payments`, and is exact only when none of the payment's events was in flight while the seed was read; to be sure, compare it with `GET /v1/payments/{id}`.

refund.description: What moved `payment.refunded_amount` for one `payment.refunded` event (Stripe Plan 4; Plan 6 Task 0c): a refund, a lost dispute, or the undoing of either. Every movement of the figure publishes exactly one event; nothing else publishes one.

amount.description: The refund's (or the dispute's) own amount (`succeeded`, `dispute_lost`), or how much the refunded figure went down (`failed`, `reversed`), base units. It can be MORE than the change of `payment.refunded_amount`: a raise is capped at the payment's amount, and a crypto refund of a document partly paid by recorded transfers counts against the transfers first. Sum `applied_amount`, never this, to follow `refunded_amount`.

applied_amount.description: How much `payment.refunded_amount` moved for this event, base units, always more than 0: up for `succeeded` and `dispute_lost`, down for `failed` and `reversed`. One refund can be two `succeeded` events with the same `id`, and a dispute's `reversed` need not match its `dispute_lost`: follow the figure by the signed sum of `applied_amount`, once per event id, never by pairing events by `refund.id`.

gateway.description: Who moved the money, as v1 names it: "solana" (a wallet, on chain) or "stripe" (the merchant's Stripe).

id.description: A card refund's `fian_ref_…`; a recorded crypto refund's id (the console's refund id); a dispute's `fian_dsp_…` (`dispute_lost`, `reversed`); for `failed`, the refund that failed.

status.description: What moved the figure; an event is published only when it moved. `succeeded`: a refund; the payment's `refunded_amount` went up by `applied_amount` (capped at `amount`). `dispute_lost`: a card dispute was lost, or a dispute already lost now reads a higher amount; the figure went up. `failed`: a refund that had succeeded failed later (a card refund, up to 30 days after) and the figure went down. `reversed`: a lost dispute was a late win (`lost` → `won`), or a dispute still lost now reads a lower amount; the figure went down. A refund that succeeds or fails while a lost dispute already covers that money moves nothing and publishes nothing; the dispute's later `reversed` carries it, so a `reversed` need not match the dispute's `dispute_lost` events.
